markdown:
## Since the last visit

Recovery is back on track after a physiotherapy lapse. Flexion has gone from 82 degrees
[2026-06-26] to 105 [2026-08-24], and the patient returned to full duties [2026-08-15].

## Current medications

- **Paracetamol** and **ibuprofen** as needed [2026-04-25]
- Oxycodone 5mg **stopped** [2026-04-25] after about eleven days, for fogginess and constipation
- Cephalexin 500mg four times daily **completed** [2026-05-06]

## What has changed

- **Flexion:** 82 degrees [2026-06-26] to 90 [2026-07-10], 98 [2026-07-25], 105 [2026-08-24].
- **Pain:** 3/10 [2026-07-10] to 2/10 [2026-07-25], now only after a long day [2026-08-05].
- **Function:** off the stick indoors [2026-07-18], stairs foot-over-foot [2026-07-25], two
  kilometres comfortably [2026-08-05], full work duties [2026-08-15].
- Mild **evening swelling** of the operated knee persists [2026-08-05].

## Worth asking about

Flexion tracked physiotherapy adherence closely. Twice-daily exercises took it from 75 degrees
[2026-05-13] to 88 [2026-05-28]. Roughly three weeks of missed sessions after returning to work
[2026-06-11] saw it fall to 82 [2026-06-26]. Resuming twice daily [2026-07-03] recovered it to 90
within a week [2026-07-10]. The patient identified the connection themselves [2026-06-19].

## Open from last time

- Once-daily exercises confirmed as appropriate at this stage [2026-08-15].
- Earlier instruction to return if wound redness spread or fever developed [2026-04-29] —
  infection resolved [2026-05-06], closed.

## The patient's questions

- When cycling can resume [2026-08-24]
- Whether evening swelling is expected this far post-operatively [2026-08-24]

flags.text: Knee flexion tracked physiotherapy adherence directly and measurably. Twice-daily exercises took flexion from 75 degrees on 2026-05-13 to 88 by 2026-05-28. Roughly three weeks of missed sessions after returning to work on 2026-06-11 saw it fall to 82 by 2026-06-26. Resuming twice daily on 2026-07-03 recovered it to 90 by 2026-07-10 and 105 by 2026-08-24.

The wound infection was identified the day after the patient reported increasing redness, warmth, discharge and a temperature of 37.9 on 2026-04-28, and was treated the same day it was assessed. Redness had pulled back by day five of cephalexin.
